title: Work IQ: invoke custom agents and agents that call third-party tools
summary: The briefing needs narrower descriptions of server and tool blocking: Microsoft now explicitly limits enforcement to governed pathways and supported gateway experiences, not every way an agent can call a server. The roadmap facts, consumption licensing and printed control paths are supported; the earlier fetch failures were not reproduced.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API equivalent for this Work IQ MCP server availability switch.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The switch controls availability of the whole Work IQ MCP server, without a governed-pathway limitation.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server (including WorkIQ MCP) blocks usage through governed Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) pathways. It doesn't automatically disable the underlying API or service endpoint outside that governed path
claims.fix: Change controls[1].governs and the rendered control label to 'Availability of Work IQ MCP through governed Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 admin center pathways'. Add to its note: 'Blocking does not automatically disable the underlying API or service endpoint outside those pathways; separate service or API policy is needed there.' Keep the existing path and docs link; cite the already-listed manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers article for this qualification.
